seoTitle: Free OpenAPI to Postman Collection Converter
metaDescription: Turn an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document, JSON or YAML, into a Postman Collection v2.1 with folders and auth. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Paste an OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document in JSON or YAML and get a Postman Collection v2.1, with requests grouped by tag, a base URL variable, parameters, example bodies and auth.
why:
An OpenAPI file describes every endpoint, but to try them you still need requests in a client. Importing the spec directly into Postman works, yet people also need a collection file they can commit to a repository, send to a tester or adjust before importing. Writing one request at a time from the spec is slow and boring.

This converter reads the spec and builds the collection for you. Operations are grouped into folders by tag, the server address becomes a baseUrl variable, parameters are listed and bodies are generated from examples or from the schema. Collection-level auth is added for bearer, basic and API key schemes. Specs often describe private services, so it helps that the conversion happens only in your browser.
howTo: Paste your OpenAPI 3 or Swagger 2 document, in JSON or YAML, into the input box.
Read the generated Postman Collection JSON in the output.
Copy it into a file, for example api.postman_collection.json.
Import the file into Postman and set the baseUrl and credentials variables.

faq.q: Does it support both Swagger 2 and OpenAPI 3?
faq.a: Yes. It reads Swagger 2 and OpenAPI 3 documents, in JSON or YAML. Very unusual features, such as complex references or callbacks, may be simplified in the generated requests.

faq.q: Where do request bodies come from?
faq.a: From the examples in the spec when present, otherwise from the schema, which gives placeholder values of the right types. Replace them with realistic data before sending requests.
Bearer, basic and API key schemes become collection-level auth with variables for the secrets. Other schemes, such as OAuth 2, are not converted, so configure them in Postman.
